- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% to avoid undershoot.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days to align with mean reversion.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.77) and price is falling, model often underestimates the decline; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast to reflect sentiment-driven volatility.
- Model frequently overestimates short-term (1–3 day) reversals; apply a 0.5–1.5% downward adjustment if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.27–0.77), model tends to lag behind true price; apply a 1–2% upward bias to forecast to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates downward trends; add 1–3% downward bias if sentiment is negative or price has recently fallen >5%.
